docker stub logs the run command as: `echo "run --name $name -p $port :: $*" >> "$LOG"` (tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py, _DOCKER_STUB `run)` case) — the log line contains `run --name` and `run -d --name` (with a space), never the literal `run-d`
The existing helper `_run_line` matches container starts via `c.startswith("run --name")` (tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:316), confirming the log token is `run --name`, not `run-d`
ABSENCE: since the substring `run-d` can never appear in the command log, the assertion passes unconditionally and does not distinguish 'no container started' from 'a container was started'
advisory.finding: The new test's assertion `not any("run-d" in c for c in cmds)` is vacuous: the docker stub logs a container start as `run --name $name -p $port :: ...` (never the contiguous substring `run-d`), so this guard is always true and cannot detect a replacement container being started against unrefreshed secrets — the very invariant its message claims to protect.
scenarios: A future regression that starts the replacement mcp container even after a fetch-secrets failure would not be caught by this assertion (the other three assertions in the test may still catch it, but this one specifically does not).
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `assert not any("run-d" in c for c in cmds)` with `assert not any(c.startswith("run --name") for c in cmds)` (or reuse `_run_line(cmds) == ""`), matching the token the docker stub actually logs.
